meta.doc: 04 §2.1 / §2.2 — the PLACEMENT rules for player-placed grid components.
meta._price_note: This file contains NO prices and quotes none, not even in a comment (report 98 C-07: one table, one place). Every dollar the placement layer spends is read at runtime from data/economy.json expenses.grid_components, which is doc 03 §2.13(b).
meta._capacity_note: This file contains NO capacities, thermal constants or protection settings. Those are doc 04 §8's data/power.json; sim/power/power_grid.gd mirrors them inline until that file lands (the P0-01 pattern). service_radius_tiles below is repeated here ONLY so the placement layer has a data source, and CitySim asserts it equals PowerGrid.TRANSFORMER_SERVICE_RADIUS at boot.
meta._scope_note: Doc 04 §4 lists place_power_component, upgrade_power_component, demolish_power_component, route_feeder, place_tie … . Wave 1.5 shipped placement of the one component that unblocks E_UNSERVED: the transformer. Wave 6 adds route_feeder (see `routable` below) and makes the two grid nodes that are BUILDINGS real (see `node_shells`). place_tie, set_feeder_underground and the arrester/flood-wall upgrades stay unshipped.
meta._roster_split_note: `placeable` is the POINT roster — one tile, one tap, one build-sheet card. `routable` is the LINE roster — a tile polyline priced per tile, the same shape doc 10's cmd_place_road and doc 05's cmd_place_water_main take, and like those it has no build-sheet card until doc 12 ships a drag tool. `node_shells` is neither: those components are placed by cmd_place_building because doc 04 §2.1 / report 98 C-30 says a substation and a plant ARE buildings.

transformer._sixth_rung_note: Wave 28 appends the SIXTH rung, 6,750 kW / radius 10 (doc 04 §2.2, doc 93 §BC-2). Every rung below is untouched. The number is derived, not chosen: it is PowerGrid.UPGRADE_MAX_R x FEEDER_CAPACITY[2] (0.90 x 7,500), the largest transformer the top conductor class can carry at doc 04 §5.3's own ceiling, so a seventh rung cannot exist without a fourth conductor class and the ladder is complete. WHY it had to exist: a building attaches to exactly one transformer, so one rung at §5.3's ceiling is the biggest load the game can serve — and at the fork 9 of doc 02's 66 published power_demand_kw cells, measured at their own doc 01 channel peak, had NO rung at all (apartment L6, office L6, high_rise L5-L6, data_center L3-L6, water_facility L5), plus doc 05's pump L5 and tank L5. Doc 92 §68.1 publishes the whole table; tests/test_balance_gates.gd::test_gate_34_every_building_fits_the_transformer_envelope is the gate that fails the moment a data edit breaks it. Doc 03 §2.13(b) prices the rung at $41,500.
transformer._placeable_levels_note: Wave 17 opens the roster to the full doc 04 §2.2 ladder, L1–L5 (50 / 150 / 400 / 1,000 / 2,500 kW). It was L1–L3 and doc 04 §6's MVP cut said L1–L4, while data/starter_city.json authors L2s and tests/fixtures/bench_city.json authors L5s — so the city the player is GIVEN ran on rungs the player could not buy. Measured with tools/audit_power.gd on the benchmark city: every one of the 140 POWER_CAPACITY blockers bound at a transformer, and 70 of them had NO purchase that cleared them because the biggest placeable transformer was 400 kW against an authored 2,500 kW. Doc 03 §2.13(b) has priced all five rungs since it shipped ($500 / $1,100 / $2,800 / $6,900 / $16,300), so this is the data edit the old note promised and not a price change (doc 91 §14.5 A91-D-55, doc 93 §AD2).
transformer._feeder_tap_note: Doc 04 §2.1 makes the transformer a child of exactly one feeder but states no tap distance, because line routing is player-drawn (report 98 C-41) and route_feeder has not shipped. Until it does, placement taps the NEAREST feeder within this radius and charges the doc 03 §2.13(b) per-tile feeder price for the lateral tiles it adds to that feeder's route (so line_km, and therefore E_grid, grow honestly). 8 is fixed twice over: it is half a 16x16 land block (constitution §6), so the utility_corridor development phase running a trunk to a block's centre puts every tile of that block — corners included — in reach of one transformer; and it is the authored starter city's own worst transformer-to-nearest-feeder Chebyshev distance, at T-05 (31,1) and T-09 (15,5), so the shipped topology is exactly reproducible by the player's own verb. Tests assert both properties against data/starter_city.json rather than against this number.

feeder._conductor_classes_note: Wave 17 opens the line roster to class 1-3 overhead for the same reason the transformer ladder opened: data/starter_city.json's own trunks are class 2 and tests/fixtures/bench_city.json's are class 3, so the authored city ran on copper the player could not buy or re-class. Doc 04 §6 deferred class 3 and this supersedes that line (doc 91 §14.5 A91-D-55, doc 93 §AD2). The per-tile price of each class is doc 03 §2.13(b)'s expenses.grid_components.feeder.cost_per_tile_overhead — $110 / $210 / $400 — and the capacities are doc 04 §2.2's, mirrored in sim/power/power_grid.gd. CitySim asserts at boot that every class listed here exists in PowerGrid.FEEDER_CAPACITY (the P0-01 pattern).
feeder._source_tap_note: Doc 04 §2.1: a feeder is rooted on exactly one substation. The run must therefore START on the network — on a tile of an existing feeder's route (branching a trunk), or within this radius of a substation building's footprint. 1 is the fence line, not a free parameter: doc 09 §2.9.5 authors SUB-A's pad at global (65,49)-(66,50) and starts BOTH authored feeders at the terminal tile (64,50), which is Chebyshev 1 from that pad, so the shipped topology is exactly reproducible by the player's own verb (tests assert this against data/starter_city.json rather than against this number).
feeder._adoption_note: The radius a newly routed feeder adopts transformers within is NOT a number of its own: it is `placeable.transformer.feeder_tap_radius_tiles` above, read at command time, because 'a transformer may tap a feeder 8 tiles away' and 'a feeder reaches transformers 8 tiles away' are the same physical statement. Adoption itself is doc 04 §2.9's transfer rule and its threshold is §8's redundancy.adoption_max_r (0.75 — §5.10's NORMAL band, deliberately NOT the 0.95 emergency auto-transfer bound), mirrored in PowerGrid.ADOPTION_MAX_R.

node_shells._note: Doc 04 §2.1 / report 98 C-30: transformers, feeders, transmission links, ties and backup generators are grid components; PLANTS AND SUBSTATIONS ARE BUILDINGS. So these two are not in `placeable` and never will be — they are placed by cmd_place_building, take their footprint from doc 02 §2.3, and the shell's sim_id IS its grid component's id (doc 09 §2.9.5 already authors it that way: the SUB-A building and the SUB-A substation node share one id). Completing the build adds the component; completing an upgrade re-rates it on doc 04 §2.2's ladder; demolishing the shell removes it. CitySim asserts at boot that every component_kind below exists in PowerGrid.CAPACITY.

priority._classes_note: Doc 04 §2.4's PRIORITY_WEIGHT ladder — 1000 / 40 / 8 / 1. Audit doc 93 §B writes the middle tier as 'PRIORITY'; the alias below accepts that spelling so the UI may use either.
